_what: Canonical spellings of corpus terms that OCR reliably mangles, with the exact variants observed. The OCR analogue of asr_vocabulary.json: same problem, different medium.
_why: A2ZERO is printed with a superscript 2. Optical recognition has no glyph for it in context and guesses -- on Year 2, 21 of 28 occurrences came back wrong as AZERO, A'ZERO or AZZERO, against 5 correct. That is the corpus's central term appearing correctly less than a fifth of the time, and no downstream alias table can fix a token that was never read as itself.
_scope: APPLIED ONLY TO OCR-SOURCED BLOCKS. Where a PDF has a real text layer its characters are authoritative, and A2ZERO printed as A²ZERO is legitimate typography to preserve verbatim, not an error to correct. Correcting an OCR misread restores what the page says; rewriting an extracted character would change it.
_never: Never a general spellcheck. Only exact variants observed in this corpus, listed explicitly, so a correction can always be traced to the reading that justified it. Every substitution made is reported, never silent.

terms.evidence: Year 2 OCR, 2026-08: AZERO x11, A'ZERO x6, AZZERO x4 against A2ZERO x5
Ann Arbor Reduce, Reuse, Return -- same superscript-adjacent styling
